Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme, and let <MATH_0002> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0003>.
Here are some standard examples of categories <MATH_0004>
that we often come up when applying
Definition <REF_0001>:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0005> is the category of all algebraic spaces over <MATH_0006>,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0007> is separated and <MATH_0008> is the category of all separated
algebraic spaces over <MATH_0009>,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0010> is quasi-separated and <MATH_0011> is the category of all
quasi-separated algebraic spaces over <MATH_0012>,
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0013> is locally separated and <MATH_0014> is the category of all
locally separated algebraic spaces over <MATH_0015>,
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0016> is decent and <MATH_0017> is the category of all decent algebraic
spaces over <MATH_0018>, and
<STRUCT_0007> <MATH_0019> and <MATH_0020> is the category of schemes over <MATH_0021>.
<STRUCT_0008>
In this case, if <MATH_0022> is a categorical quotient then we say
<MATH_0023> is
(1) a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>categorical quotient<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>,
(2) a <TEXTITOPEN_0002>categorical quotient in separated algebraic spaces<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>,
(3) a <TEXTITOPEN_0003>categorical quotient in quasi-separated algebraic spaces<TEXTITCLOSE_0003>,
(4) a <TEXTITOPEN_0004>categorical quotient in locally separated algebraic spaces<TEXTITCLOSE_0004>,
(5) a <TEXTITOPEN_0005>categorical quotient in decent algebraic spaces<TEXTITCLOSE_0005>,
(6) a <TEXTITOPEN_0006>categorical quotient in schemes<TEXTITCLOSE_0006>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme, and let <MATH_0002> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be a full subcategory of the category of algebraic
spaces over <MATH_0005> closed under fibre products.
Let <MATH_0006> be pre-relation in
<MATH_0007>, and let <MATH_0008> be an <MATH_0009>-invariant morphism with
<MATH_0010>.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> We say <MATH_0011> is a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>universal categorical quotient<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
in <MATH_0012> if for every morphism <MATH_0013> in <MATH_0014>
the morphism <MATH_0015> is the categorical quotient in
<MATH_0016> of the base change <MATH_0017> of <MATH_0018>.
<STRUCT_0003> We say <MATH_0019> is a <TEXTITOPEN_0002>uniform categorical quotient<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>
in <MATH_0020> if for every flat morphism <MATH_0021> in <MATH_0022>
the morphism <MATH_0023> is the categorical quotient in
<MATH_0024> of the base change <MATH_0025> of <MATH_0026>.
